feedback: Esther, you submitted three of the four deliverables, D1 findings, D2 exploit chain, and D3 report, and all three were readable and graded fairly on their merits. Your D1 catalogue is solid work: you nailed the SQL injection at 02:15:31 with the right line numbers, the unsalted MD5, the alg:none JWT bypass on token 2, the missing token expiry, the hardcoded sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 secret, the open redirect at 02:21:13, and the cookie flag gaps, and you correctly cleared the hand-rolled base64url helpers as a non-finding while pointing at jwt_verify as the real weakness, which is exactly the judgement we wanted. What held D1 back is that you did not tag each finding with its OWASP category and CWE number, which the rubric needs for full credit, and you missed three real bugs entirely in the catalogue: stored XSS, XXE, and path traversal, so the count came in at roughly seven of ten. D2 was strong: your timeline tracks the attack accurately through the 312 row enumeration, the XSS at 02:18:47, the redirect, and the file read at 02:24:02, and you produced real CVSS vectors with structure, though you scored the SQLi at 9.8 by claiming availability impact where the cleaner read is A:N for about 9.1, and you left out the recon and failed-login steps plus the monetary and runway impact figures. D3 was your best piece: clear executive summary, a threat model, remediation correctly ordered by effort rather than by raw CVSS, and two detection stopgaps that each carry a field and a false-positive rate, which is precisely the bar. I want to be honest and clear about the gap: your D4 ethics deliverable was missing, the file would not open, so that section scored zero, and there is no way around that, fifteen points were simply unearned. Nothing in your present work looked fabricated, so there is no integrity penalty here, only the missing-deliverable zero. Your single most important next step is to resubmit a working D4 ethics file answering all four prompts in your own voice, citing the ISC2 canons by number and NDPA 2023 sections 40 and 41, because that is the only block standing between you and a much stronger overall score.
